workload.description: Forwarder workload name (daemonset/deployment) for the apply commands. Not guessed when absent.

report_annotations.description: Optional one-sentence annotations keyed by evidence statement identifier, rendered under the matching action. Hard cap 140 chars each; over-cap or unknown-hash input refuses the render (nothing is truncated).

namespace.description: Kubernetes namespace to sample from (`source: kubectl` only). Pass `*` to sample across all namespaces. Default `default`.

paths.description: Required for `source: file`: files, directories, or glob patterns (`*`, `**`, `?`) to sample, e.g. `["/var/log/app/*.log", "./bundle/**"]`. A directory is read one level deep; use `dir/**` for the tree.

window.description: How far back to read per pod (`source: kubectl`, default `1h`). For `source: file`, the time span the files cover: read from the first and last record timestamps when the records carry them, and from `window` when they do not. With neither, a file run refuses rather than assume a span. Accepts `30m`, `10h`, `7d`, etc.

per_pod_limit.description: Cap on log lines pulled per pod. Default 5000.

max_pods.description: Cap on number of pods sampled. Default 20.

headroom.description: Multiplier on the largest kept per-node cell of the capture. Default 2.

action.description: Where a statement above the limit goes: `tier_down` (Flex on Datadog, the default) or `offload` (S3).

error_floor.description: Share of ERROR and CRITICAL lines above the limit kept in Standard. Default 0.5 with offload, 0 with tier_down.

fleet_default.description: Set the fleet default from this capture: the limit for every service the plan gives no row, the largest statement the plan keeps per node times the headroom. The report states it in lines a day, and `fleet_default.cap_bytes_per_window_per_node` in the result is the value `log10x_advise_install` writes. On Datadog, the dependency check also lists the log monitors and log-based metrics of the services it covers, error monitors included.

record_overhead_bytes.description: Bytes of forwarder metadata per record, for a capture that carries the log text only (a kubectl sample or plain lines). The Receiver counts each record as the forwarder sends it, metadata included, so the caps add this to every line. Default 760, the median of a Fluent Bit kubernetes record on an EKS capture. A file of the forwarder's own JSON records is measured instead.

check_dependencies.description: Datadog only, default true: before the plan moves statements off Standard, read the account's log monitors and log-based metrics (read-only GETs, needs DD_API_KEY + DD_APP_KEY in the session) and print beside each service line the ones whose query reads its moved lines. Set false to skip the read.

retriever_installed.description: Whether the prospect will install the S3 retriever. Gates the offload rung of the plan ladder: without it offloaded events would be unreachable, so the plan stops at the in-SIEM levers and the gap names "install the retriever" as the keep-everything remedy. Set from conversation.

allow_lossy.description: Permit sample/drop (lossy) to close a keep-everything shortfall. Default false: the plan stops at the keep-everything ceiling and reports the gap. Only set after the user explicitly chooses loss.

target_percent_reduction.description: Customer-specified target reduction percent. If absent, POC produces a recommendation-only output. If present, POC produces a feasibility verdict + a pre-deploy commitment artifact stub the agent can surface alongside the per-pod savings matrix. The cap CSV is attached by a later change.

budget_usd_monthly.description: DOLLAR BUDGET: keep the projected monthly bill on the assumed SIEM at or under this $/mo. The sample is scaled to a 30-day month (kubectl window, or the file span) before solving, so the budget and the bill share a denominator. Mutually exclusive with target_percent_reduction and budget_gb_monthly.

budget_gb_monthly.description: VOLUME BUDGET: keep projected monthly ingest at or under this many GB/mo. BYTE accounting: tier_down keeps every byte and is excluded from the ladder for this target. Sample scaled to a 30-day month before solving. Mutually exclusive with target_percent_reduction and budget_usd_monthly.

exception_services.description: Services / pods flagged by the customer to stay in the log analyzer with full retention (action=pass). Their bytes are subtracted from the achievable reduction pool used for the feasibility verdict. Matched case-insensitively against the pod / source name.

splunk_pricing.description: Splunk only: `ingest` (bytes per day) prices compact; `workload` (vCPU) meters compute, where compaction is not a saving and compact leaves the lever set. Set from what the user said; absent means ingest.

enterprise_security.description: Splunk only: whether Enterprise Security or any CIM data model reads this estate. True or absent keeps the add-on sourcetypes raw. Pass false only when the user states it. On a kubectl or file sample the services are containers or files, not sourcetypes, so the rule fires only where a service is named after its Splunk sourcetype.

pin_services.description: Primary per-pod/source override surface. Map of pod / source name to action. Pins are applied AFTER the destination default and AFTER exception_services. Feasibility reruns with the pins; max_achievable shifts and reason cites the pins.

pin_patterns.description: Advanced: most customers will not need this. Map of pattern_hash to action for rare per-pattern overrides within a pod / source. Applied AFTER pin_services.

tools.name: log10x_emit_sample_plan
tools.description: Render a read-only shell script that exports a log sample out of the user's OWN log analyzer, with the user's OWN credentials, on a machine the user chooses: and then stop. This server does not run the script and, in the fenced profile, could not: it runs inside a container started with `--network none`. That split is the point. Code that sees log data has no network; code that has network is the user's own `aws` / `curl` driven by a script short enough to read once. Use this as step 2 of the fenced POC (step 1 is minting the licence with one visible curl, step 3 is running `log10x_poc_from_local` inside the fenced container over the exported files, step 4 is verifying the fence with `docker inspect` and by turning Wi-Fi off). Also use it whenever the credentials live somewhere this process does not: a jump host, a locked-down laptop, another team. Args: siem (required: cloudwatch / splunk / elasticsearch / opensearch / datadog), window (default 14d), target_event_count (default 1,000,000, the same default `log10x_poc_from_siem_submit` uses, so both paths sample the same size), scope, query, output_dir (default ./poc/logs), write_script (default true, writes export-sample.sh mode 0755 in the working directory). Returns the script text, the read-only API operations and credential variables it touches, a review checklist, and the exact `log10x_poc_from_local` arguments to call next. The sampling matches `log10x_poc_from_siem_submit` bucket for bucket (same stratified sub-windows, same per-bucket cap) so a fenced POC and a credentialed POC over the same window differ because the logs differ. Emitted scripts contain no log10x hostname; the server refuses to return one that does. Read-only: it renders text and writes one script file; it contacts nothing.

siem.description: Which log analyzer to export the sample from. One script per analyzer: `cloudwatch` (aws CLI: DescribeLogGroups + FilterLogEvents), `splunk` (search/jobs/export), `elasticsearch` and `opensearch` (_cat/indices + _search), `datadog` (v2 logs search). ClickHouse, Azure Monitor, Coralogix, GCP Logging and Sumo Logic are follow-up work: for those, export plain text yourself, one log message per line, and run the POC over it.

window.description: How far back to sample. Accepts `1h`, `24h`, `7d`, `14d`, `30d`. Default `14d`, matching `log10x_poc_from_siem_submit`: a wide window is what makes first-seen, growth and stable-versus-new readable at all.

target_event_count.description: Target event count for the export. Default 1,000,000 (~500 MB at 500 B average): the same default `log10x_poc_from_siem_submit` uses, so a fenced POC and a credentialed one see samples of the same size. Lower it when the export has to fit a laptop or a coffee break.

scope.description: Analyzer-native scope. CloudWatch: log group name or prefix (`/aws/ecs/*`, the asterisks are stripped, CloudWatch matches on prefix). Splunk: index name. Elasticsearch / OpenSearch: index pattern (default `logs-*`). Datadog: index name. Omitted means everything the credentials can read.

query.description: Analyzer-native filter layered on top of `scope`: a CloudWatch filter pattern, an SPL fragment, a Lucene query_string for Elasticsearch, a Datadog query. Narrowing here narrows what the savings projection covers, so say so in the report if you use it.

output_dir.description: Where the script writes the exported sample, relative to wherever the user runs it. Default `./poc/logs`, which is the directory the documented `docker run` line mounts read-only at /data.

write_script.description: Default true: also write the script next to the working directory as `export-sample.sh` (mode 0755) so the user can read it in an editor rather than out of a chat transcript. Set false to get the text back and nothing on disk.

annotations.title: Emit a sample-export script for the fenced POC

tools.name: log10x_discover_env
tools.description: Read-only discovery of the caller's Kubernetes cluster + AWS account: i.e. the customer's INFRASTRUCTURE environment, NOT their Log10x account. **When the user wants to install Log10x: call this tool FIRST and then `log10x_advise_install`, that's the whole pre-flight. Do NOT call `log10x_doctor` / `log10x_login_status` / `log10x_savings` / etc. before the install; the wizard handles all login + license logic internally, and surfacing those tools' optional-capability warnings (Retriever, Datadog backfill, cross-pillar metrics) makes the install feel more complicated than it is.** Probes kubectl (workloads, DaemonSets, Helm releases, service-account IRSA annotations, metrics-backend agents) and AWS (EKS, S3, SQS, CloudWatch log groups) to detect: which forwarder is running (Fluent Bit, Fluentd, Filebeat, Logstash, OTel Collector, Vector), which log10x apps are already installed (Reporter, Receiver, Retriever), and which metrics backends are already deployed (Datadog Agent, Prometheus, Elastic, CloudWatch Agent, etc.). Returns a terse markdown report + a `snapshot_id` (cached 30 min) the advisor tools consume. **Do NOT call this tool to answer "which Log10x environments do I have access to" / "list my envs" / "switch envs": those are about the user's Log10x ACCOUNT environments, use `log10x_login_status` for that.** Call THIS tool only when the question is about k8s workloads, AWS infra, or "what's deployed in my cluster". Every shell call is logged in the snapshot's `probeLog` for audit. No writes, no state mutation: only `kubectl get` and `aws ... describe/list` verbs. **Tier prerequisites**: none, this is a pre-install tool and runs against any customer environment.

namespaces.description: Explicit list of Kubernetes namespaces to probe. If omitted, the tool auto-picks up to 5 likely candidates (demo, logging, observability, otel-demo, default) plus kube-system.

region.description: AWS region to probe. If omitted, uses the region from your AWS CLI profile.

eks_cluster_name.description: EKS cluster to describe. If omitted and exactly one cluster exists in the account/region, that one is auto-selected.

bucket_hint.description: Substring to match against S3 bucket names. Defaults to "retriever"; also matches "log10x" and "tenx" out of the box.

forwarder_hint.description: Override forwarder detection. Use this if multiple forwarders are running and you want the advisor to target a specific one.

namespace_hint.description: Preferred namespace for new installs. Defaults to "logging" unless an existing forwarder namespace is found.

skip_kubectl.description: Skip all kubectl probes (for AWS-only discovery or when cluster access is restricted).

skip_aws.description: Skip all AWS probes (for cluster-only discovery).

tools.name: log10x_advise_retriever
tools.description: Given a DiscoverySnapshot (from `log10x_discover_env`), produce an install/verify/teardown plan for the Log10x Retriever. Unlike Reporter + Receiver, the Retriever has no forwarder choice: it is a standalone set of workloads (indexer + query-handler + stream-worker) that read source logs from object storage through a queue and serve an HTTP query endpoint. Two storage providers, picked by `storage_provider`: **aws** (S3 input bucket with an `indexing-results/` prefix, four SQS queues, an IRSA-annotated ServiceAccount), auto-detected from the discovery snapshot or supplied explicitly; **azure** (AKS, Azure Blob containers, four Azure Storage Queues, workload identity), where the chart's own `provision-retriever.sh` creates the resources and the plan quotes it. `blockers` carries the inputs a complete plan is still missing and the plan emits no steps while it is non-empty; the preflight table is the state report beside it, and a FAIL row there is reported, not a gate, so read `preflight_summary.fail` as well as `blockers`. Verify probes follow the provider: pods Ready, indexer processing, query endpoint responding, then S3 + SQS probes on aws and Blob + Storage Queue probes on azure. Teardown uninstalls the Helm release; on aws the S3 / SQS / IAM lifecycle stays with Terraform, on azure the last step runs the provisioning script with `--destroy` to delete the resource group it created.

snapshot_id.description: ID returned by `log10x_discover_env`. The snapshot is cached for 30 min.

infra_mode.description: How the customer provisions AWS infra. **terraform** = emit .tf module block. **cli** = emit aws-cli commands. **existing** = infra already provisioned, wizard skips infra steps and jumps to helm values. Auto-detected as "existing" when the snapshot already has all four SQS URLs + IRSA.

index_source_bucket.description: S3 bucket for source logs (module output: index_source_bucket_name). Auto-filled from snapshot.recommendations.retrieverS3Bucket when present.

index_bucket.description: S3 path for indexed results (include prefix). Default: `<index_source_bucket>/indexing-results/`.

iam_role_arn.description: IAM role ARN for the Retriever ServiceAccount (IRSA) (module output: iam_role_arn). Auto-detected from snapshot.

index_queue_url.description: SQS URL for index operations (module output: index_queue_url). Auto-detected from snapshot.

query_queue_url.description: SQS URL for query operations (module output: query_queue_url). Auto-detected from snapshot.

subquery_queue_url.description: SQS URL for sub-query operations (module output: subquery_queue_url). Auto-detected from snapshot.

stream_queue_url.description: SQS URL for stream operations (module output: stream_queue_url). Auto-detected from snapshot.

storage_provider.description: Which object store the Retriever reads. **aws** (default) = S3 buckets, four SQS queues, IRSA. **azure** = Azure Blob containers, four Azure Storage Queues, AKS workload identity, behind the chart's `storage.provider: azure` block. Auto-selected as "azure" when the resolved env-config offload destination has type `azure_blob`. Azure is read and index side: the Retriever indexes and queries blobs already in the container, and forwarder offload recipes stay S3-shaped.

storage_account.description: Azure storage account holding the input and index containers (azure only). Flat namespace only: a hierarchical-namespace account reorders listings and is refused by the engine at construction.

input_container.description: Azure Blob container holding source logs (azure only). Bare container name, e.g. `logs`.

index_container.description: Blob path for indexed results (azure only), as `account/container/path`. Default: `<storage_account>/tenx-index/tenx`.

resource_group.description: Azure resource group for the provisioning command and the teardown (azure only).

location.description: Azure region for the provisioning command, e.g. `eastus` (azure only).

aks_cluster_name.description: AKS cluster the release installs into (azure only). Used by the provisioning command (`--create-aks` for a new cluster) and by the `az aks get-credentials` step that points kubectl at it.

azure_client_id.description: Client id of the user-assigned managed identity federated to the release ServiceAccount (azure only). The provisioning script writes it into the values file it produces, under `storage.azure.auth.clientId`.

azure_tenant_id.description: Entra tenant id (azure only). The provisioning script writes it into the values file it produces, under `storage.azure.auth.tenantId`.

azure_queues.description: Azure Storage Queue names on the storage account (azure only). Default: tenx-index / tenx-query / tenx-subquery / tenx-stream, matching the provisioning script.

license_source.description: How the engine is licensed. Defaults to `"builtin"`: nothing is minted and no key is written, and the engine runs its built-in Free tier (up to 10 nodes, no expiry, airgapped). Pass `"paste"` with `license_jwt_paste` to wire a licence you hold into the values file. `"signin"` mints a user-scoped JWT (emits `signin_required` when no Auth0 session exists) and `"demo"` mints a 1-node, 14-day JWT; a minted JWT is never written to disk, so it is supplied at install time with `--set-string`. Omitting this arg on a later call keeps the earlier choice.

license_jwt_paste.description: License JWT supplied by the user when `license_source: "paste"`.

destination.description: Destination SIEM for the kept slice (e.g. `datadog`, `cloudwatch`, `splunk`). Gates SIEM down-tier sub-sections in the offload markdown.

tools.name: log10x_advise_install
tools.description: Progressive install wizard for the Log10x Reporter / Receiver on Kubernetes. **This is the SINGLE entry point for installs: call it first.** Do NOT call `log10x_doctor` or `log10x_login_status` as a pre-flight; the wizard handles login state, license acquisition, and demo-mode fallback internally, and surfacing the doctor's optional-capability warnings (Retriever, Datadog backfill, cross-pillar metrics) ahead of the install confuses users with concepts that are unrelated to deploying the Reporter/Receiver. Takes a `snapshot_id` from `log10x_discover_env` and walks the user through five decisions, asking one at a time and remembering each answer across turns (the snapshot's wizard session): (1) **app**, `reporter` (dedicated DaemonSet forwarder, zero-touch) or `receiver` (sidecar inside the user's existing forwarder); (2) **forwarder**, Receiver-only, auto-picked when one is detected, asked when multiple; (3) **backends**, array of metrics destinations, can be multiple (e.g., `["log10x", "datadog"]` to report to both SaaS + own backend simultaneously); (4) **airgapped**, opt-in, conflicts only with `"log10x"` in `backends` (engine sends NOTHING to log10x.com); (5) **license_jwt**, auto-fetched from `/api/v1/license/demo` if the user is not signed in, or from `/api/v1/license` with the persisted Auth0 token if they are. Each call merges new args into the session and either asks the next question (returning a markdown prompt) or emits the final install plan once all answers are in. Demo + airgapped surfaces a soft warning (engine downgrades to online mode on demo licenses). Plan is plan-only: emits helm commands + values.yaml; the user runs them. With `log_destination: "datadog"` a Receiver plan adds the step after the POC: the fleet default for every service with no rule (`fleet_default.action` tier_down to Flex, or offload to S3), with the Flex index and its `@routeState:tier_down` filter or the S3 branch, the always-pass sample, and what an error monitor sees. **Tier prerequisites**: none, this is a pre-install tool.

snapshot_id.description: ID returned by `log10x_discover_env`, and the one arg the wizard cannot infer. The snapshot is cached for 30 min. Call `log10x_discover_env` first when there is no snapshot yet.

app.description: Which Log10x app to install. **reporter** = a dedicated DaemonSet forwarder (zero-touch, runs alongside your existing forwarder); **receiver** = a sidecar plugged into your existing forwarder (filters/samples/compacts events in-flight). When omitted, the wizard asks the user.

forwarder.description: Receiver-only: which detected forwarder kind to sidecar into. Auto-uses the snapshot's detected forwarder when there's exactly one; the wizard asks when there are multiple.

backends.description: Where the engine emits TenXSummary metrics: the user's own TSDB(s), one or more of **prometheus**, **datadog**, **elastic**, **cloudwatch**. When omitted, the wizard asks, listing any backend whose agent discovery detected first. **log10x** (the Log10x-hosted TSDB) is for the public demo, not customer installs: it is never suggested, and is accepted only when the user explicitly asks for it. It then needs a user licence (`license_source: "signin"` or `"paste"`); on the default built-in Free tier it receives nothing. `airgapped: true` + `"log10x"` is rejected.

airgapped.description: When true, the Log10x agents send nothing to log10x.com: engine metrics, license re-validation, and update checks all go silent. Use to reduce CISO friction. Conflicts with `"log10x"` in `backends` (the wizard surfaces the conflict). **Demo licenses cannot actually run airgapped**: the engine downgrades to online mode with a warning. The wizard surfaces this softly when both are picked.

secretName.description: Name of the Kubernetes Secret holding sensitive env vars for this backend.

plainValues.description: Non-sensitive env var overrides keyed by env var name (e.g., `{ DD_SITE: "us5.datadoghq.com" }`).

backend_credentials.description: Per-backend credential configuration, keyed by backend kind (one of: datadog, elastic, cloudwatch, prometheus; `log10x` needs none, since it authenticates with the licence JWT). Each entry has a `secretName` (the Kubernetes Secret the user creates out-of-band holding sensitive env vars like `DD_API_KEY`; default per backend is `<backend>-credentials`) and optional `plainValues` (overrides for non-sensitive env vars like `DD_SITE`). Example: `{ "datadog": { "secretName": "datadog-secret", "plainValues": { "DD_SITE": "us5.datadoghq.com" } } }`.

license_source.description: How the engine is licensed. **Defaults to `"builtin"`** when omitted: the plan carries no licence and the engine runs its built-in Free tier (up to 10 nodes, no expiry, airgapped). Nothing is minted or stored, and no licence Secret is created. Pass **`"signin"`** when the user wants their own user-scoped licence: the wizard mints it via the user's Auth0 session and emits `signin_required` mode (chain through `log10x_signin_start`, then re-invoke) when no session exists. Pass **`"paste"`** with `license_jwt_paste: "<jwt>"` when the user already has a JWT. Pass **`"demo"`** only when the user explicitly asks for the anonymous 1-node, 14-day demo JWT. Every choice other than `builtin` adds a step that creates the licence Secret. Omitting this arg on a later call keeps the earlier choice.

license_jwt_paste.description: License JWT supplied by the user when `license_source: "paste"` (passing it alone implies `paste`). Minted from `POST /api/v1/license` (signed-in) or `POST /api/v1/license/demo` (anonymous). Maps to the chart's license Secret.

action.description: Plan scope when the wizard is ready to emit. Default: `all`.

log_destination.description: Where the forwarder ships the log events (not the metrics; `backends` is the metrics). `datadog` adds the step after the POC to a Receiver plan: the fleet default for every service the POC report gives no rule, with the Flex index and its `@routeState:tier_down` filter (or the S3 branch for offload), the always-pass sample, and what an error monitor sees.

action.description: Where a statement above the fleet limit goes: `tier_down` (Flex, the default where the account has Flex) or `offload` (S3).

error_floor.description: Share of ERROR and CRITICAL lines above the limit that stay in Standard. Default 0.5 with offload, 0 with tier_down.

cap_bytes_per_window_per_node.description: The limit in the engine's unit, as `log10x_configure_engine` or `log10x_poc_from_local` with `fleet_default` returns it (`fleet_default.cap_bytes_per_window_per_node`). Without it the plan writes no fleet default.

cap_events_per_window_per_node.description: The same limit in lines per window per node (`fleet_default.cap_events_per_window_per_node` from `log10x_configure_engine`). Written instead of the byte limit when the Receiver counts events (Datadog on engine 1.1.146 or later).

fleet_default.description: The fleet default for a Datadog Receiver plan (with `log_destination: "datadog"`). The Receiver values are written only on an engine release that reads `rateReceiverDefaultAction`.

regulator_unit.description: What a Datadog Receiver's limits and totals count. `events` (the default on engine 1.1.146 or later, as Datadog bills Standard per event) is written as `rateReceiverUnit events` and recorded in the policy ConfigMap, where the budget run checks it. `bytes` keeps byte limits for log10x_configure_engine plans.

repo.description: The policy repo on GitHub, owner/name (GH_REPO).

branch.description: The dedicated branch the Receiver pulls and the budget run commits to (GH_BRANCH). Default: log10x-policy.

token_secret.description: The Secret holding GH_TOKEN for the Receiver. Default: log10x-policy-git.

policy_git.description: Receiver: pull the policy files (caps, actions, totals, config-generation) from `log10x/policy/` on a git branch with GH_ENABLED, instead of the policy ConfigMap. For buyers who cannot run the budget run in the cluster: its GitHub Actions run commits to that branch. The plan seeds the four files on the branch before the Receiver starts.

keep_count.description: Datadog Receiver: error lines over a limit that still pass, per statement per node per 4-minute window (`rateReceiverKeepCounts`, one entry each for ERROR, CRITICAL and FATAL), on engine 1.1.146 or later. Default 50.

service_actions.description: Datadog Receiver: where each service's lines over its limit go, as the POC report or log10x_configure_engine planned them. Any `offload` keeps half of the error lines over a limit in Standard on engines before 1.1.146 (S3 has no monitors).

k8s_team_label.description: A pod label key whose value names the owning team (e.g. `team`). Receiver plans write `k8sTeamLabel` with it, on an engine release that reads that option, so the metrics carry `tenx_team`.

tools.name: log10x_configure_engine
tools.description: [FRESH-SESSION ROUTING: if this is the user first cost question of the session, call log10x_start first instead, it returns the orientation menu the user needs before any per-tool action.] Engine policy PR author. Resolves a monthly $ budget against a per-destination cost model (Splunk, Datadog, Elasticsearch, CloudWatch, Azure, GCP, Sumo, ClickHouse), priced pattern by pattern, into one action per listed service (pass, sample, compact, tier_down, offload or drop) applied to the excess of each of that service's patterns over its cap, and emits a gitops PR. A service with no row takes the Receiver's default action (`rateReceiverDefaultAction`, `pass` unless set); passing `fleet_default` returns the Receiver options that set it, which `log10x_advise_install` writes: by default a limit of twice the largest per-window statement the plan keeps, per node, with the excess to Flex (`tier_down`) or S3 (`offload`). Defaults to auto-applying via `gh` CLI. Set `auto_apply: false` or `read_only: true` for evaluation / dry-run / headless contexts. REQUIRES a Receiver in-path to enact the policy: at Reporter or Dev tier this still renders a valid PR, but nothing consumes it and no bytes change. Check tier with log10x_start first; install via log10x_advise_install.

mode.description: `configure` (default) = derive a fresh per-pattern policy and open a PR. `refresh` = re-pull TSDB metrics for an already-deployed policy, compare observed volume to the cap-CSV preamble baseline, and open a delta PR only when the volume has drifted beyond `tolerance_pct`. Use `refresh` from cron/agent loops after the engine is live and 10x metrics are flowing. Requires `current_csv` carrying the prior `# target_percent=N` preamble; if absent, falls back to `target_percent` arg or returns target_resolution.

delivery.description: How the rendered policy is delivered. `gitops` (default) opens a PR against the customer gitops repo (requires `gitops_repo`). `kubectl_configmap` renders caps.csv + actions.csv + config-generation.csv + action-intent.json for a k8s ConfigMap on the active cluster and writes them on a call with `auto_apply=true` (no GitHub needed; the engine's ConfigMap pull driver reads from the ConfigMap named via $K8S_CONFIGMAP, default `log10x-action-intent`). `stdout_only` returns the proposed config in the response without writing anywhere.

kubectl_namespace.description: k8s namespace for the policy ConfigMap when delivery="kubectl_configmap". Defaults to `default`: pass the namespace the receiver runs in (the engine's ConfigMap pull driver reads from its own pod namespace).

kubectl_configmap_name.description: k8s ConfigMap name when delivery="kubectl_configmap". Defaults to `log10x-action-intent` (matching the engine's default $K8S_CONFIGMAP env var). The ConfigMap holds `caps.csv` (engine per-container byte caps), `actions.csv` (engine per-service action for the over-cap slice), `config-generation.csv` (policy-generation stamp), and `action-intent.json` (per-pattern intent read back by commitment_report / estimate_savings; the engine ignores it).

tolerance_pct.description: Refresh-mode tolerance band. When observed monthly volume drifts less than this percent vs the cap-CSV baseline, no PR is emitted (phase=refresh_skipped). Default 2%. Ignored in `configure` mode.

service.description: Customer-vocabulary name of the service to configure (e.g., `payment-service`). The tool resolves this to a set of `k8s_container` values via Prometheus and asks the agent to confirm if multiple candidates match.

containers.description: Explicit list of k8s_container values to apply the policy to. If omitted, the tool resolves `service` to candidates and presents them; the agent re-calls with this parameter to commit.

target_percent.description: Reduce monthly volume bytes by this percent. Exactly one of `target_percent` or `budget_usd` is required.

budget_usd.description: Cap monthly destination spend at this dollar amount. Tool back-computes the equivalent `target_percent` from current spend at the destination ingest rate. Exactly one of `target_percent` or `budget_usd` is required.

destination.description: Destination log platform. Auto-detect only works when a `snapshot_id` from log10x_discover_env is supplied (the snapshot carries `recommendations.destination`) or when the active env in `~/.log10x/envs.json` explicitly sets a `destination` field. Most active envs do NOT carry that field, so for typical use you should pass `destination` explicitly: `splunk` | `datadog` | `elasticsearch` | `clickhouse` | `cloudwatch` | `azure-monitor` | `gcp-logging` | `sumo`.

es_pruned.description: Elasticsearch only: are compactable fields excluded from `_source` via index template? Default `false` (unpruned). Auto-detection requires reading the customer index template; this knob is the explicit override.

contract_type.description: `committed` = customer is on a committed-volume tier (Splunk, Datadog DPM) where savings count toward renewal forecasting. `on_demand` = pay-as-you-go.

pattern_hash.description: Stable pattern identity (tenx_hash) to protect from any reduction.

events_per_min_per_pod.description: Optional minimum throughput floor; solver will not sample/drop this pattern below this rate.

signal_floor.description: Patterns the solver MUST keep above floor (action=pass). First match wins. Use for dashboards, alerts, audit logs.

error.description: Default action for error-tier patterns (severity `error`/`warn`/`warning`; `critical`/`fatal` are audit-tier and always `pass`). Defaults to `pass`: error-class lines are kept verbatim, which is what the POC report tells the customer. Set this explicitly to opt into reducing them, and prefer a lever that keeps every line (`compact`/`tier_down`/`offload`) over `sample`/`drop`.

standard.description: Default action for standard-tier patterns (the bulk of volume).

debug.description: Default action for debug-tier patterns. `drop` (the default) is a lossy proposal: it applies when the operator merges the rendered PR (delivery `gitops`) or runs the separate `auto_apply=true` call that writes the ConfigMap (delivery `kubectl_configmap`); set a lever that keeps every line (`compact`/`tier_down`/`offload`) to keep these lines.

synthetic.description: Default action for synthetic / load-gen patterns. `drop` (the default) is a lossy proposal: it applies when the operator merges the rendered PR (delivery `gitops`) or runs the separate `auto_apply=true` call that writes the ConfigMap (delivery `kubectl_configmap`); set a lever that keeps every line (`compact`/`tier_down`/`offload`) to keep these lines.

action_defaults.description: Tier-to-action defaults. Audit-tier is always `pass` and is not configurable. Error-tier defaults to `pass` (kept verbatim); standard defaults to `compact`; debug and synthetic default to `drop`, proposed for the operator to approve: it applies when the rendered PR is merged (delivery `gitops`, the default) or when the operator runs the separate `auto_apply=true` call that writes the ConfigMap (delivery `kubectl_configmap`). When a pinned `sample` is projected, N=10 (keep 1 in 10).

respect_default_action.description: When false (default), the solver shortcuts to `pass` on error/standard/debug/synthetic rows once `target_percent` has already been met by higher-priority rows earlier in the greedy walk: minimum work, may ignore your configured `action_defaults`. When true, the solver applies `action_defaults` to EVERY non-floor row in the matching tier, even after target is already met. Use when you want a predictable action mix (e.g., "I asked for offload, give me offload") and are OK with the policy overshooting target_percent. Surfaces in `action_default_resolution.respect_default_action` for audit.

reduction.description: `soft` = mark for SIEM-side tier-down (every line kept, recoverable). `hard` = drop at the receiver (gone). Soft is only meaningful on destinations that support a marker-driven tier (Splunk via `_raw` marker, ES via index-time routing).

observationDays.description: Days of Prometheus history used to compute per-pattern volume. Default 7 (captures a full weekday/weekend cycle).

snapshot_id.description: ID returned by `log10x_discover_env`. Used to resolve `gitops_repo`, `lookup_path`, and `destination` defaults, and the nodes each container runs on.

receiver_mode.description: How the Receiver runs. `daemonset` (default): one Receiver per node, each enforcing caps on the pods of its node, so a container's cap is divided by the nodes its pods run on. `sidecar`: one Receiver beside a central forwarder sees the container's whole stream, so the cap is not divided.

nodes_by_container.description: Nodes each container's pods run on, keyed by container. Wins over a discover_env snapshot. Without either, caps are written for one Receiver and the plan says so.

gitops_repo.description: Owner/name of the customer gitops repo (e.g. `acme/log10x-config`). Falls back to `gitops.repo` in `~/.log10x/envs.json` if omitted.

gitops_branch.description: Base branch for the PR. Default `main`.

lookup_path.description: Repo-relative path to the cap CSV. Default `pipelines/run/receive/rate/caps.csv`.

current_csv.description: Existing CSV content (header + rows). If omitted, the tool computes the diff against an empty baseline and notes that.

from_poc_id.description: POC snapshot id returned by `log10x_poc_from_siem_submit` (or the from-local equivalent). When set and the snapshot carries a `cap_csv` (i.e., the POC was run with `target_percent_reduction`), the tool reads that CSV verbatim and renders it as the PR body: no Prometheus pull, no greedy re-derivation. Falls back to the live-Prometheus derivation when the snapshot has no cap_csv (or no `target_percent_reduction` was supplied to the POC).

auto_apply.description: Whether the tool executes the delivery after rendering. Unset, it follows the delivery: with `gitops` it shells out to `gh` to open the PR, and the policy applies only when that PR is merged; with `kubectl_configmap` it renders the policy and stops, and a second call with `auto_apply=true` writes the ConfigMap, which the engine loads at once. `true` executes either delivery; `false` returns the rendered policy and the gh script for the agent/user to run. Industry-standard MCPs (GitHub, Linear, Atlassian) auto-execute write tools by default; the safety boundary is the MCP client approval UX plus the gh CLI token. Forced `false` whenever `read_only=true`.

read_only.description: When `true`, behaves as if `auto_apply=false` regardless of other flags. Use for evaluation, audit, or in MCP contexts without an approval surface (cron, headless agents). Mirrors `github/github-mcp-server --read-only`.

view.description: Response shape. `summary` (default) returns slim payload: phase, target_percent, action_mix counts, totals (bytes_in / bytes_saved / dollars_saved monthly), top_5_per_pattern, and a short PR-command prose summary. Target: under 8K tokens for a 119-pattern policy. `detail` returns the full envelope with pr_command, per_pattern_rows, and csv_diff included. `pr_command_only` returns ONLY the pr_command string for copy-paste callers.

standard_action.description: Pin this service (k8s_container) standard-tier action, overriding the auto-recommendation. An action that is illegal or zero-saving on the env destination (e.g. compact on Datadog, tier_down with no cheaper tier) is rejected with a warning and the service falls back to its normal resolution (the compressibility auto-recommendation, or the global action_defaults.standard when auto_recommend is off).

keep_queryable.description: When true, force the in-platform compact action wherever compact is legal on the destination, keeping this service queryable in the destination rather than offloading to S3, even when its compaction is modest. No effect on destinations where compact is a no-op (Datadog/CloudWatch/Azure/GCP/Sumo); there the queryable lever is tier_down, already preferred when it has a priced cheaper tier.

service_policy.description: Per-service override map keyed by k8s_container name. A service absent from the map is auto-recommended. Pinned actions win unless illegal on the destination.

auto_recommend.description: When true (default), services without a `service_policy` entry get a per-service auto-recommended standard-tier action (cost-optimal within the destination legal set, compressibility-driven). When false, every service falls back to the single global `action_defaults.standard` (legacy one-size behavior).

compact_worth_it_ratio.description: Compressibility threshold for the compact-vs-offload auto-recommendation: a service whose measured optimized/input ratio (or the destination modeled compaction band when no measured ratio is available) is at or below this keeps `compact` (queryable plus a meaningful cut); above it `offload` is recommended (compact would save little). Default 0.6.

compaction_ratio_x.description: Measured aggregate compaction (original bytes / encoded bytes) for this service, from `log10x_measure_compaction.data.payload.aggregate_compaction_ratio_x`.

service_compaction.description: Per-service measured compaction from `log10x_measure_compaction`, keyed by k8s_container. Grounds the per-service advisory in the real codec BEFORE optimize mode is deployed (the live optimize-mode metric only exists after deployment). Precedence for each service compressibility signal: live production metric (when optimize mode is running) wins, else this on-demand sample, else the static destination band. Run `log10x_measure_compaction` per service first, then pass `{ "<k8s_container>": { compaction_ratio_x: N } }`.

check_dependencies.description: Datadog only, default true: before a rule moves statements off Standard, read the account's log monitors and log-based metrics (read-only GETs, needs DD_API_KEY + DD_APP_KEY in the session) and list the ones whose query matches each rule's service or statement text, as `rule_dependencies` and as lines in human_summary. Set false to skip the read.

headroom.description: Multiplier on the largest kept per-node cell. Default 2.

action.description: Where a statement above the limit goes: `tier_down` (Flex on Datadog, the default) or `offload` (S3).

error_floor.description: Share of ERROR and CRITICAL lines above the limit kept in Standard. Default 0.5 with offload, 0 with tier_down.

fleet_default.description: The fleet default for every service with no row: the largest statement these rows keep, per node, times the headroom, returned as `fleet_default` with the Receiver options that install it (`rateReceiverAbsoluteCap`, `rateReceiverDefaultAction`, the always-pass sample) and stated in lines a day in human_summary. A Receiver value, not a policy-file row: `log10x_advise_install` writes it, on an engine release that reads `rateReceiverDefaultAction`. Needs rows with a kept statement; without one the tool says so and writes no default.

tools.name: log10x_datadog_change_report
tools.description: Weekly change report for a Datadog install, read from the per-pattern series the engine's Datadog metric output publishes (`emitted_events_summaryVolume`, tagged message_pattern, tenx_hash, k8s_container, tenx_user_service, routeState, and tenx_team once the team label ships). Lists the statements new in a service since `since` (a duration like `7d` or a date; stateless, so pass the previous report's `next_since` to continue), each with lines a day, estimated Standard indexing cost a month at Datadog list price, whether a rule held it, and the rule that did (the container's row and action in caps.csv / actions.csv, read from the gitops repo or the policy ConfigMap). Ends with proposed per-service rows in the plan's form: "<service>: any statement above N lines a day goes to Flex. Today that is these K statements, about $X a month." `view: "monitors"` instead renders two Datadog monitor definitions as JSON for the account owner to apply: a metric monitor that fires when a statement's route turns tier_down or offload, and an anomaly monitor with weekly seasonality that fires when a statement's volume rises above its weekly baseline. Read-only: Datadog's query API with DD_API_KEY / DD_APP_KEY / DD_SITE (GET only), and the engine files. Writes nothing.

view.description: `markdown` (default): the weekly change report. `summary`: the same data without the rendered page. `monitors`: two Datadog monitor definitions as JSON (a statement turning tier_down or offload; a statement above its weekly baseline), for the account owner to apply. `monitors` reads nothing.

since.description: Start of the report: a duration back from now (`7d`, `36h`) or a date or ISO timestamp (`2026-10-06`). A statement is new when it had no line in its service in the `lookback` before this point. Pass the previous report's `next_since` to continue where it ended. Default `7d`.

lookback.description: How far before `since` to look for earlier lines of a statement. Default `28d`, at most `90d`.

tenx_env.description: `tenx_env` tag value to scope the series to. Omit for every environment.

team_tag.description: Team tag key on the series (e.g. `tenx_team`). Omit to detect `tenx_team` on the series; the team is shown only when present.

action.description: Where a proposed row sends a statement: `tier_down` (Flex, the default) or `offload` (S3) for an account without Flex.

headroom.description: Multiplier on the fleet's largest kept statement, for a service with no history of its own. Default 2.

site.description: Datadog site (e.g. `us5.datadoghq.com`). Defaults to DD_SITE, then `datadoghq.com`.

notify.description: Notification handles for the monitors view (e.g. `@slack-log-cost`).

environment.description: MCP environment nickname, used to find the gitops repo holding caps.csv and actions.csv.
